newsitem.title: USA: Navistar in tentative pact to extend UAW contract. [CORRECTED 21:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Navistar in tentative pact to extend UAW contract. [CORRECTED 21:00 GMT]

text.p: Navistar International Corp. Wednesday said it reached a tentative agreement to extend its master contract with the United Auto Workers union until Oct. 31, 2002, a deal it said will allow it to build a new medium duty truck in Springfield, Ohio.

The agreement, which covers about 8,000 (corrects from 11,000) Navistar employees, is subject to a ratification vote by the UAW membership this weekend. It also is contingent on the approval of funding for a new truck program. The program will be reviewed at the company's August board meeting, with funding expected to be approved in October, Navistar said.
Navistar's current contract is scheduled to run out Oct. 31, 1998.
Aside from allowing the company to build its next-generation truck in Springfield, the agreement will maintain production at its Indianapolis foundry, Navistar said.

The ability to build the new truck "is quite positive for the company," said Eli Lustgarten, analyst at Schroder & Co. But he also said it was too early to comment on the contract, because he did not know its terms, including whether the truck and engine maker received concessions on staffing at its Springfield facilities.
Navistar would not comment on terms of the contract. A UAW spokesman was not immediately available.
The tentative contract helped boost Navistar shares $1.31 to $21.875 at mid-afternoon.
Navistar also said it reached a tentative agreement with Ford Motor Co. to continue to supply diesel engines for some Ford pickup trucks and Econoline vans.
The new 10-year agreement would be effective beginning with model year 2003. Navistar will produce a newly designed and advanced technology engien for Ford, the companies said.
